棕榈油为什么常被称为热带毁林的"隐形推手"？

Why is palm oil often called the invisible driver of tropical deforestation?

它便宜又用途广，从饼干到洗发水都有，巨大需求推动热带雨林改种油棕；因藏在无数产品里，消费者很难在货架上"看见"它。
Cheap and everywhere—from biscuits to shampoo—its huge demand converts rainforests to oil palm; hidden in countless products, shoppers rarely "see" it on the shelf.

全球供应链的环境成本，为什么常常"看不见"？

Why are global supply chains' environmental costs often "invisible"?

污染和毁林发生在生产端、好处却在消费端，地理与账本都把它们隔开了；我们买到便宜货，代价却由远方的空气、水土和人或默默承担。
Pollution and deforestation happen at production while benefits land at consumption, separated by distance and accounting; we get cheap goods while distant air, water and people quietly pay.

一件衣服的"碳足迹"，为什么常常跨越好几个国家？

Why does a single garment's carbon footprint often span several countries?

棉花可能在甲国种、布在乙国织、衣在丙国缝、再运到丁国卖；每一段运输与生产都排碳，于是你身上的衣服"走过"半个地球。
Cotton may grow in A, cloth weave in B, sew in C and sell in D; each leg of transport and production emits, so your clothes "travel" half the globe.

为什么"本地消费"不一定比"进口"更环保？

Why isn't "local consumption" automatically greener than "imported"?

关键看全链条：本地大棚冬天靠加热种菜，碳可能高于南方田间直运；运输只占部分排放，生产方式往往更重要，"本地"不是万能标签。
It depends on the whole chain: local winter greenhouse heating can emit more than field-to-shelf transport from the south; transport is only part of emissions, so "local" isn't a magic label.

你喝的一杯咖啡，为什么可能和远方的森林砍伐有关？

Why might your cup of coffee be linked to distant deforestation?

部分咖啡种在毁林开垦的种植园，你支付的价钱里有对远方土地的需求；消费选择会沿着供应链传到产地，改变一片林的生死。
Some coffee grows on deforested plantations, so your payment carries demand to distant land; consumption choices travel the supply chain and decide a forest's fate.
